issues: Minor: fit_predict trains the MLPs on the standardized target (y - mu) / sd but returns np.mean(preds) without converting back (* sd + mu). Spearman depends only on rank order, and this rescaling keeps the order, so the loss is unaffected and this is no reason to veto. It does break the contract that the function returns the predicted value in the original units. Fix it if this design is kept.

This is a borderline result. The incumbent rests on a single run, and z of about 1.64 is right at a one-sided 5% threshold. The change is one simple line, so accepting it is reasonable. A replicate of the incumbent would make the comparison firmer.

Minor point: KernelRidge has no intercept term. Fitting rank targets in (0,1] without centering them adds a shrink-toward-zero effect. This has no effect on correctness. Centering y by subtracting 0.5 might help a little.

Memory and runtime risk. Each training fold has about 776 molecules and 1228 kept columns. If minmax_kernel builds a full (n, m, d) broadcast array, that is about 5.9 GB in float64 and would go over the 6 GB limit. A kernel built from loops or matrix products is fine. Ten bags × 2 kernels × 15 fits should fit inside 10 minutes if the kernel is vectorised efficiently.
